subject: Sales engineering SLO handshake — latency targets, concurrency & demo timeline
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@helixlabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30T15:12:00Z
Subject: Sales engineering SLO handshake — latency targets, concurrency & demo timeline

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call + a few asks to make the hosted vs incumbent comparison productive. This is focused on end-to-end p95/p99 SLA qualification for your production path (client -> API -> model -> render).

What we heard (please confirm):
- Target end-to-end p95: ~200 ms
- Target end-to-end p99: ~450 ms (tail is currently the main blocker)
- Sustained throughput target: ~500 requests/sec across peak region (US-East)
- Concurrent streaming sessions during peak: ~120 (many sessions are long-lived streaming chat)
- Typical request payload: user prompt + 3-shot context, average tokenized input ~110 tokens, output average ~60 tokens

Asks / next steps so we can scope demos and canary:
1) Share a 24-hour traffic profile (attached suggested csv) and a sample of real request payloads or anonymized traces (sample format below).
2) Confirm which endpoints matter for SLO (chat-stream vs batch-generate vs embeddings).
3) Give us a preferred demo/canary week — we proposed 2028-07-07 below; if we get traffic profile + traces by EOD 2028-07-02 we can provision a faithful test.
4) Any hard constraints on tokenization/timeouts, e.g., client timeouts under 800 ms?

Attachment: traffic_profile_v1.csv (format: timestamp,endpoint,req/s,avg_input_tokens,avg_output_tokens)

I'll coordinate a short prep call with our performance eng (Karthik) once we have sample traces.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

--
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference platform
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@helixlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Sales engineering SLO handshake — latency targets, concurrency & demo timeline

Thanks, Soojin — great summary and yes, that captures our goals. A few clarifications from our side:
- p95/p99 targets are for the full client-visible E2E time (including our SDK + network + model). The incumbent reports p99 spikes up to ~1.1s during nightly batch writes; we are most concerned about the daytime peak tail.
- Endpoints: prioritize chat-stream and chat-generate. Embeddings matter for offline workflows only.
- Token lengths: on the rare side we have long context sessions (up to ~600 tokens in), but 90% of traffic is under 160 tokens in.

Attached: helix_traces.jsonl (anonymized traces with request_id, endpoint, start_ts, end_ts, input_tokens, output_tokens) — should help.

We can target the week of 2028-07-07 for a demo/canary. Procurement looped in (procurement@helixlabs.com) for timelines and PO.

Alex Jones
Senior Product Manager — Platform
HelixLabs
alex.jones@helixlabs.com

> Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call + a few asks to make the hosted vs incumbent comparison productive. This is focused on end-to-end p95/p99 SLA qualification for your production path (client -> API -> model -> render).
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Sales engineering SLO handshake — latency targets, concurrency & demo timeline

Looping in some initial engineering thoughts after quick pass on helix_traces.jsonl. Key clarifications we need before scheduling an infrastructure-accurate canary: 

- Endpoint mapping: are chat-stream and chat-generate the same backend path or separate services? If separate, we should run two concurrent canary patterns.
- Tail cause hypothesis: traces show spikes correlated with large output tokens (>>300). Is the incumbent doing synchronous decoding for those or throttling?
- Network contribution: can Helix confirm average client-to-edge RTT in ms by region (we need to subtract realistic network baseline to set model runtime targets).

Proposed internal action items:
1) Soojin: request Helix send representative SDK timeout settings and any edge proxies used (e.g., CDN, gateway).
2) Naomi: prepare a shadow load plan that mimics Helix peak envelope (500 rps with 120 long-lived streams).
3) Karthik: baseline quantized candidate models for token-length distribution and estimate decode time at 160/300/600 token outputs.

We should also include a short pre-canary call (30m) to align on test harness and data handling.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@helixlabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, procurement@helixlabs.com
Date: 2028-07-01T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Sales engineering SLO handshake — latency targets, concurrency & demo timeline

Alex — appreciate the quick turnaround and the traces. Proposed concrete plan and acceptance criteria so we can lock a demo slot: 

1) Timeline
- 2028-07-02: Helix sends final traffic profile + SDK timeouts + edge RTTs
- 2028-07-03: Redwood performance team validates traces and confirms canary config
- 2028-07-07: Canary/demo window (2 hours) against hosted environment

2) Acceptance criteria (initial):
- p95 end-to-end <= 220 ms for chat-generate under your daytime traffic envelope
- p99 end-to-end <= 500 ms (we expect some tail; this is the first gate)
- No more than 5% error rate and streaming session connection timeouts below 1%

3) Canary test shape
- Sustained: 500 rps across chat-generate endpoints for 10 minutes
- Burst windows: 1 minute spikes to 900 rps to validate autoscaling behavior
- Long-lived streaming: 120 concurrent streaming sessions, 10% of them producing outputs >300 tokens

Attachments: slo_acceptance_checklist.pdf (checklist + metrics dashboard links)

Logistics: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567. I can reserve 2028-07-07 16:00-18:00 EDT for the demo; please confirm. If procurement needs a separate procurement cadence, procurement@helixlabs.com is looped.

If you confirm the traffic profile by 2028-07-02 EOD we will proceed with provisioning infra and a short sync on 2028-07-03.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134
